06a_10_negative_control.png: The negative control. Left: the part proportional to $a_4'$ of the coefficient of $\gamma^{(x4)}$ in $\gamma^\mu\Omega_\mu$ versus the rate $a_4'$, both in units of $H = 1$, for the corrected metric, whose hidden block deflates (solid, the line $-a_4'/2$), and for a control metric whose hidden block grows like 3-space (dashed, the line $+7a_4'/2$); the part $b_4'/b_4$ is the same in both. Right: the coefficient of $\gamma^{(x0)}$ versus the time $x_4$ on the history $a_4 = x_4$, $b_4 = e^{4x_4/3}$ on a logarithmic axis: $\frac32e^{x_4/3}$ for the author's metric and $\frac32e^{-5x_4/3}$ for the control, in both cases $\frac32H$ divided by the scale factor of the hidden block. The term sees in which direction the hidden block changes.
06a_1_polar_frame_and_spin_rotation.png: Warm-up in the flat plane. Left: the unit radial direction (black) and the unit angular direction (orange) of the polar frame at twelve angles on the circles $r = 1$ and $r = 2$, drawn in Cartesian coordinates $x$, $y$ (pure numbers); the frame turns by the angle $\varphi$ as one goes around, and the spin connection $\omega_{\varphi 01} = -1$ records this rate. Right: the entry $U_{11} = \cos(\varphi/2) + i\sin(\varphi/2)$ of the spinor rotation $U$ that carries the Cartesian frame into the polar frame (its inverse $U^{-1}$ removes the connection), real part (solid) and imaginary part (dashed), for $\varphi$ from $0$ to $4\pi$; at $\varphi = 2\pi$ the spinor rotation is $-1$, and only at $4\pi$ is it $+1$ again.
06a_2_vielbein_factors.png: The factors $f_a$ of the diagonal vielbein of the corrected metric. Left: versus the time $x_4$ in units $1/H$ at $z = \pi/4$, on the history of the Revision record $a_4 = x_4$, $b_4 = e^{4x_4/3}$, on a logarithmic axis; the 3-space factor $e^{a_4}$ grows, the hidden factor $s_b\cot z = e^{-x_4/3}$ and the extra-time factor $s_bW$ shrink side by side at one third of that exponential rate, the time factor is $1$, and the 7-volume factor $e^{-a_4}b_4^2|\cot z|W^3$ grows like $e^{5x_4/3}$. Right: versus the hidden angle $z = 6Hx_0$ in radians across one cell; the warp factor $W = (\sin^2 z)^{1/12}$, the hidden factor $|\cot z|$ and the volume factor divided by $e^{-a_4}b_4^2$, which both vanish at the fold $z = \pi/2$ (vertical line).
06a_3_christoffel_pattern.png: Where the Christoffel symbols $\Gamma^l{}_{mn}$ of the corrected metric are nonzero: one 8 x 8 grid per upper index $l = x0, \dots, x7$, rows $m$ and columns $n$ numbered 0 to 7 for $x0$ to $x7$, each square coloured by the sign of the symbol at the sample point $H = 1$, $z = \pi/4$, $a_4 = 1/2$, $a_4' = 1$, $b_4 = e^{2/3}$, $b_4'/b_4 = 4/3$ (on the history of the Revision record; red positive, blue negative, white zero). Every nonzero symbol has an index equal to 0 or 4: the metric depends only on the hidden coordinate $x_0$ and on the time $x_4$; the 3-space directions 1, 2, 3 meet only the time. The grids are symmetric because $\Gamma^l{}_{mn} = \Gamma^l{}_{nm}$.
06a_4_omega_heat_maps.png: The canonical spin connection $\omega_{\mu ab}$ of the diagonal vielbein as three heat maps, for $\mu = x0$ (left, the hidden direction), $\mu = x1$ (middle, an inflating 3-space direction) and $\mu = x5$ (right, a deflating extra time), at the sample point $H = 1$, $z = \pi/4$, $a_4 = 1/2$, $a_4' = 1$, $b_4 = e^{2/3}$, $b_4'/b_4 = 4/3$ (on the history); rows $a$ and columns $b$ are the frame directions $x0$ to $x7$, the colour and the printed number give the value (red positive, blue negative, white zero). Each array is antisymmetric, and only the pairs with $x4$ or $x0$ are nonzero; the hidden direction and the extra time turn towards the time with the same negative rate $h_4 = -1/3$, the 3-space direction with the positive rate $a_4' = 1$.
06a_5_spinor_connection_heat_maps.png: The spinor connection $\Omega_{x0}$ (left), $\Omega_{x1}$ (middle) and $\Omega_{x5}$ (right) as 16 x 16 heat maps at the sample point $H = 1$, $z = \pi/4$, $a_4 = 1/2$, $a_4' = 1$, $b_4 = e^{2/3}$, $b_4'/b_4 = 4/3$; rows and columns are the 16 spinor components, red is positive, blue negative, white zero, each panel with its own colour scale. $\Omega_{x0}$ and $\Omega_{x1}$ are boosts (a space-like direction with the time), symmetric matrices (entries $(i, j)$ and $(j, i)$ of the same colour); $\Omega_{x5}$ is a rotation of two time-like directions, antisymmetric, plus a boost. All three map the first eight components to the first eight and the last eight to the last eight.
06a_6_gamma_omega_per_direction.png: The eight terms $\gamma^\mu\Omega_\mu$ (no sum) of the diagonal vielbein, each equal to $\alpha_\mu\gamma^{(x4)} + \beta_\mu\gamma^{(x0)}$; horizontal axis the direction $\mu$ (red: inflating 3-space, blue: the hidden block of $x0$ and the three extra times, gray: time). Left: the part of $\alpha_\mu$ proportional to $a_4'$, in units of $a_4'$: $+1/2$ for $x1, x2, x3$ and $-1/2$ for $x0, x5, x6, x7$, total $-1/2$. Middle: the part proportional to $b_4'/b_4$, in units of $b_4'/b_4$: $1/4$ for each direction of the hidden block, total $1$. Right: $\beta_\mu$ in units of $He^{a_4}b_4^{-1/2}$: three times $1/2$, total $3/2$. So $\gamma^\mu\Omega_\mu = \frac32He^{a_4}b_4^{-1/2}\gamma^{(x0)} + (b_4'/b_4 - a_4'/2)\gamma^{(x4)}$.
06a_7_gamma_omega_sum.png: The sum as pictures of 16 x 16 matrices at the sample point $H = 1$, $z = \pi/4$, $a_4 = 1/2$, $a_4' = 1$, $b_4 = e^{2/3}$, $b_4'/b_4 = 4/3$ (on the history of the Revision record) (red positive, blue negative, white zero; colour scale from $-2$ to $2$). Top left: the sum of the three 3-space terms, $\frac32 a_4'\gamma^{(x4)}$ with entries $\pm 1.5$; top right: the sum of the four terms of the hidden block $x0, x5, x6, x7$, $2h_4\gamma^{(x4)} + c_g\gamma^{(x0)}$ with $2h_4 = -2/3$ and $c_g = 1.77$ on two diagonal lines; their $\gamma^{(x4)}$ parts have opposite signs and do not cancel. Bottom left: the total over all eight directions; bottom right: $c_g\gamma^{(x0)} + v_g\gamma^{(x4)}$ with $v_g = 5/6$. The two bottom pictures are identical.
06a_8_divergence_form.png: The divergence form of $\gamma^\mu\Omega_\mu$, with $H = 1$, checked by central differences with step $10^{-5}$. Left: the coefficient $c_g$ of $\gamma^{(x0)}$ divided by $e^{a_4}b_4^{-1/2}$, $\partial_{x0}(\sin^2 z)^{1/4}/(2\cot z\,(\sin^2 z)^{1/4})$, versus the hidden angle $z$ in radians across both halves of a cell (the vertical line is the fold): the constant $3/2$ for every $z$. Right: the coefficient of $\gamma^{(x4)}$, $\partial_{x4}(e^{-a_4}b_4^2)/(2e^{-a_4}b_4^2)$, versus the time $x_4$ for $a_4 = x_4$ and the illustrative function $b_4 = e^{4x_4/3}(1 + \frac12\sin x_4)$ (solid), on the exact $b_4'/b_4 - a_4'/2$ (dotted), and $5/6$ for the history $b_4 = e^{4x_4/3}$ of the Revision record (dashed): the time term is half the rate of the 7-volume $e^{-a_4}b_4^2$.
06a_9_derivative_coefficients.png: The factors $1/f_a$ in front of the derivatives in the Dirac operator $\gamma^\mu D_\mu = \sum_a f_a^{-1}\gamma^{(a)}\partial_a + c_g\gamma^{(x0)} + v_g\gamma^{(x4)}$. Left: versus the time $x_4$ in units $1/H$ at $z = \pi/4$ on the history of the Revision record $a_4 = x_4$, $b_4 = e^{4x_4/3}$, on a logarithmic axis: the 3-space factor $e^{-a_4}$ falls, while the hidden factor $e^{a_4}b_4^{-1/2}\tan z$ and the extra-time factor $e^{a_4}b_4^{-1/2}/W$ rise like $e^{x_4/3}$; this is how the deflation of the hidden block enters the field equation. Right: versus the hidden angle $z$ in radians at $x_4 = 0$ across one cell: the hidden factor $|\tan z|$, unbounded at the fold (vertical line), and the factor $(\sin^2 z)^{-1/12}$ of the extra times.
